questions.stem: Which of the following enzymes acts as the rate-limiting step in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) by cleaving liver-derived angiotensinogen to generate angiotensin I?

options.text: Renin
Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE)
Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2)
Neprilysin (NEP)

questions.stem: A 58-year-old male with long-standing hypertension and chronic kidney disease is started on an ACE inhibitor. Which intracellular signaling pathway is primarily activated by Angiotensin II binding to the Angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor (AT1R) to induce efferent arteriolar vasoconstriction?

options.text: Adenylate cyclase activation leading to intracellular cAMP accumulation
Gq/11 coupling to Phospholipase C (PLC), generating IP3 and DAG to increase intracellular Ca2+
Gi activation leading to inhibition of protein kinase A and nitric oxide release
Receptor tyrosine kinase autophosphorylation activating the Ras/Ref/MAPK pathway

questions.stem: Which counter-regulatory axis of the renin-angiotensin system utilizes ACE2 to convert Angiotensin II into Angiotensin-(1-7), producing vasodilation, natriuresis, and anti-fibrotic effects via the Mas Receptor?

options.text: AT1R - Gq/11 Axis
PRR - VDR Axis
ACE2 - Ang-(1-7) - MasR Axis
Neprilysin - Endothelin-1 Axis

questions.stem: In the Zona Glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex, which terminal enzyme catalyzes the conversion of 11-deoxycorticosterone to aldosterone through successive 11-beta-hydroxylation, 18-hydroxylation, and 18-oxidation?

options.text: CYP17A1 (17-alpha-hydroxylase)
CYP21A2 (21-hydroxylase)
CYP11B1 (Steroid 11-beta-hydroxylase)
CYP11B2 (Aldosterone synthase)

questions.stem: Under normal physiological conditions, which enzyme in the Aldosterone-Sensitive Distal Nephron (ASDN) metabolizes cortisol to inactive cortisone, preventing cortisol from inappropriately occupying and activating the Mineralocorticoid Receptor (MR)?

options.text: 11-beta-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase Type 2 (11-beta-HSD2)
11-beta-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase Type 1 (11-beta-HSD1)
5-alpha-Reductase Type 2
Glucuronosyltransferase 1A1

questions.stem: Which early aldosterone-induced gene product phosphorylates and inactivates the E3 ubiquitin ligase Nedd4-2, thereby stabilizing apical membrane density of the Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC)?

options.text: WNK4 kinase
Serum- and Glucocorticoid-Regulated Kinase 1 (SGK1)
Protein Kinase C alpha
Calcineurin A alpha

questions.stem: Regarding the 'Aldosterone Paradox', how does high Angiotensin II during hypovolemia allow the kidney to maximize sodium reabsorption while minimizing renal potassium wasting?

options.text: Angiotensin II inhibits ENaC channels directly in the cortical collecting duct.
Angiotensin II activates WNK4 to phosphorylate NCC in the DCT and dephosphorylates MR Ser-843 in Type A intercalated cells.
Angiotensin II degrades ROMK potassium channels via lysosomes in principal cells.
Angiotensin II upregulates 11-beta-HSD2 activity in renal vascular smooth muscle.

questions.stem: In the setting of isolated hyperkalemia with low circulating Angiotensin II, what molecular alteration in Intercalated Cells of the distal nephron prevents aldosterone-mediated chloride reabsorption, thereby favoring potassium excretion?

options.text: Phosphorylation of the Mineralocorticoid Receptor at Serine-843 (Ser-843)
Dephosphorylation of the ENaC alpha subunit at Serine-550
Ubiquitination of Pendrin (SLC26A4) transporters
Proteolytic cleavage of ROMK channels by prostasin

questions.stem: Neprilysin (NEP, CD10) is a membrane-bound zinc metallopeptidase. Which of the following bioactive peptides is NOT a substrate degraded by Neprilysin?

options.text: Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP)
B-type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP)
N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP)
Bradykinin

questions.stem: Why did single-agent Neprilysin inhibitors (such as Candoxatril) fail to produce effective vasodilation and blood pressure reduction in clinical hypertension trials?

options.text: Inhibition of Neprilysin causes a compensatory increase in renal 11-beta-HSD2 activity.
Inhibition of Neprilysin prevents Angiotensin II degradation, causing reflex accumulation of Angiotensin II that opposes natriuretic peptides.
Neprilysin inhibitors directly block NPR-A receptors on vascular smooth muscle cells.
Neprilysin inhibitors accelerate renal ENaC subunit assembly

questions.stem: Which drug combination rationale underlies the dual Angiotensin Receptor-Neprilysin Inhibitor (ARNI) class (Sacubitril / Valsartan)?

options.text: Sacubitril inhibits Neprilysin while Valsartan blocks the AT1R to prevent accumulated Angiotensin II action.
Sacubitril inhibits ACE while Valsartan activates the Mas Receptor.
Sacubitril inhibits Aldosterone Synthase while Valsartan blocks ENaC channels.
Sacubitril stimulates eNOS while Valsartan inhibits renal 11-beta-HSD1.

questions.stem: Why is the concurrent administration of an ACE inhibitor (e.g., Enalapril) and a Neprilysin inhibitor strictly contraindicated, requiring a mandatory 36-hour washout period when switching to ARNI?

options.text: Synergistic inhibition of aldosterone leading to immediate cardiac arrest from hyperkalemia
Dual blockade of Bradykinin breakdown leading to severe, life-threatening Angioedema
Irreversible inhibition of renal proximal tubule brush border dipeptidases causing Fanconi syndrome
Complete suppression of erythropoietin synthesis leading to acute aplastic anemia

questions.stem: What is the intracellular second messenger activated downstream of Natriuretic Peptide Receptor-A (NPR-A) when ANP or BNP binds to vascular endothelial and renal tubular epithelial cells?

options.text: Inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3)
Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)
Cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)
Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH)

questions.stem: A 65-year-old patient with diabetic kidney disease and an initial eGFR of 45 mL/min/1.73m2 is started on an ACE inhibitor. Two weeks later, repeat lab tests show serum creatinine increased from 1.5 mg/dL to 1.7 mg/dL (eGFR dip of 15%). Serum potassium is 4.8 mEq/L. What is the appropriate clinical management?

options.text: Discontinue the ACE inhibitor immediately due to acute renal failure.
Continue the ACE inhibitor without dose reduction and recheck renal function in 2-4 weeks.
Switch from the ACE inhibitor to a loop diuretic immediately.
Perform emergency bilateral renal arteriography.

questions.stem: Which landmark clinical trial demonstrated that Sacubitril/Valsartan reduced the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization by 20% compared to Enalapril in patients with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF)?

options.text: PARADIGM-HF
PARAGON-HF
FIDELIO-DKD
DAPA-CKD

questions.stem: In the UK HARP-III trial evaluating Sacubitril/Valsartan versus Irbesartan in patients with chronic kidney disease (eGFR 20-60 mL/min/1.73m2), what was the key finding regarding renal safety and hemodynamic parameters?

options.text: Sacubitril/Valsartan caused significantly higher rates of end-stage renal disease than Irbesartan.
Sacubitril/Valsartan demonstrated comparable renal safety while achieving superior blood pressure and cardiac biomarker reduction.
Sacubitril/Valsartan caused severe unmanageable hyperkalemia requiring trial termination.
Sacubitril/Valsartan induced irreversible proximal tubular necrosis.

questions.stem: How does Finerenone, a non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), differ structurally and pharmacologically from steroidal MRAs like Spironolactone?

options.text: Finerenone acts as an agonist at the progesterone receptor.
Finerenone exhibits high selectivity with bulky non-steroidal MR binding, resulting in lower hyperkalemia rates and minimal sex-hormone side effects.
Finerenone irreversibly inhibits renal proximal tubule NHE3 exchangers.
Finerenone requires bioactivation by adrenal Zona Reticularis cytochrome enzymes.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical scenarios presents the highest risk of acute hemodynamic eGFR drop greater than 30% upon initiating an ACE inhibitor or ARB?

options.text: Bilateral renal artery stenosis or unilateral renal artery stenosis in a solitary kidney
Primary hyperaldosteronism due to Conn syndrome
High dietary sodium intake with minimal diuretic therapy
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in early stage

questions.stem: Which renal tubule segment and channel are primarily targeted by atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) to promote natriuresis and diuresis?

options.text: Inhibition of Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter (NKCC2) in the Thick Ascending Limb
Inhibition of Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC) in the Inner Medullary Collecting Duct (IMCD)
Stimulation of SGLT2 cotransporter in the Proximal Convoluted Tubule
Inhibition of Pendrin Cl-/HCO3- exchanger in Type B Intercalated Cells

questions.stem: A 62-year-old female with HFrEF and Stage 3b CKD taking Sacubitril/Valsartan and Finerenone presents with serum potassium of 5.7 mEq/L. She is asymptomatic with normal ECG. Which conservative management step should be performed FIRST to maintain cardiorenal therapy?

options.text: Permanently discontinue both Sacubitril/Valsartan and Finerenone immediately.
Assess dietary potassium, eliminate concurrent NSAIDs, and initiate a modern potassium binder (e.g., SZC or Patiromer).
Administer emergency intravenous calcium gluconate and insulin-dextrose infusion.
Initiate acute hemodialysis via a temporary femoral catheter.
